transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because... for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, bills show up wrong, and people just happen to forget to call me back. 

Everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes or clerical errors, but... I know they’re keeping information from me. It's clear that they're trying to push me out of making decisions.
Do you feel that there’s a deliberate effort by others, maybe even a group or organization, to prevent you from accessing information or making decisions?

Yes, that’s exactly what I mean. Like I was just saying, it’s... it's just too much of a pattern to be an accident. 

When you see the exact same things happening over and over—her appointments getting moved, the bills constantly being wrong, people conveniently forgetting to return my calls—it's clearly deliberate. They can call it a mistake all they want, but I know they are purposely keeping information from me so they can push me out of making any decisions.
Have you ever felt that something others believe to be true is actually not true, or that you know something others don’t realize at all?

Yes, well, that goes right back to what I was just explaining. Everyone else—the staff, my family—they all believe these are just innocent clerical errors. They think it's completely normal for bills to be wrong or for appointments to just get shuffled around by accident. 

But I know that's not true. I know for a fact that they are doing it on purpose to keep me in the dark. They don't realize that I can see right through it. I know they are actively coordinating this to push me out of making any decisions for my sister, even if they all swear up and down that it's just a coincidence.
Have you ever experienced things that others around you don’t seem to notice, like hearing voices, seeing things, or sensing something that isn’t actually there?

No, I haven't had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My mind is perfectly sound. I just see the pattern in the paperwork and the scheduling—the actual, tangible things that are happening right in front of me. It's not my imagination.

Have you ever tried to explain your concerns to others, and even when they didn’t agree or showed you evidence against it, did you still firmly believe that the pattern you’re seeing was intentional and meant to keep you out of the decision-making?

Yes, absolutely. I've tried explaining it to my family and the staff at the facility. Like I mentioned before, for months now I've been pointing out this pattern with my sister's appointments and the bills. 

They always have some excuse ready. They’ll try to show me a schedule or say they were just short-staffed, or claim it was a computer glitch. But even when everyone insists it’s just mistakes, I don't buy it. I supervise an administrative office for a living, so I know what real clerical errors look like, and this isn't it. 

No matter what they say or try to show me, I know they’re keeping information from me. I know they are doing it to push me out of making decisions for her, and nothing they say is going to change what I see happening right in front of me.
Even when people have shown you explanations, like computer errors or staffing issues, do you still believe, without any doubt, that this is a coordinated effort to keep you from making decisions?

Yes, without a doubt. I mean, like I said, I'm here because this has been going on for months. I see the exact same pattern over and over. Her appointments get moved around, the bills show up with all these errors on them, people conveniently forget to call me back. 

They can tell me it's a computer error or a staffing issue all they want, but I know what I'm looking at. Even when everyone around me says they're just honest mistakes, I know they are keeping information from me. They are deliberately trying to push me out of making decisions for my sister. I have absolutely no doubt about it.
